title: Gotcha Day
text: The day Maya picked me out of a crate of six puppies. I was the one chewing her shoelace. She said that is how she knew.

title: First Bath
text: Maya laughed so hard she cried. I was so mad. I shook all over her and she laughed even harder.

title: The Mail Carrier
text: Every day at 11:15 I warn Maya about the mail carrier. Every day she says he is our friend. I remain unconvinced.

title: Sprinkler Season
text: The summer Maya ran through the sprinklers with me in the front yard. The neighbors stared. We did not care.

title: Tennis Ball Champion
text: Maya threw the ball 47 times in a row. I brought it back 46 times. The 47th is still in the pond. I think about it often.

title: Bodega Bacon
text: The bodega guy gives me a strip of bacon every Sunday. Maya pretends not to see. This is our secret.

title: Fireworks Night
text: I was scared of the fireworks, so Maya sat with me on the roof and covered my ears with her hands until it was over.

title: The Big Move
text: The day we moved to the city, Maya carried me up five flights of stairs because I was too nervous to climb them.

title: Pup Cup
text: Maya ordered me a pup cup on my birthday and the whole cafe sang. I wore a paper crown. I was magnificent.

title: Sunrise Walk
text: The morning Maya could not sleep, so we walked to the water and watched the sun come up together.

title: Yarn Disaster
text: I unraveled the scarf Maya was knitting for her mom. She was not mad. She just started over and let me hold the end.

title: Car Window
text: Head out the car window on the highway, ears flying, Maya singing badly to the radio. Perfect.

title: Rainy Day
text: Thunder all afternoon. Maya built a blanket fort and we watched cartoons until it passed.

title: Night Light
text: Maya leaves the hallway light on for me. She thinks I am afraid of the dark. I am a little.

title: Belly Rubs
text: There is a spot on my belly that makes my leg kick. Only Maya knows exactly where it is.

title: Sick Day
text: When Maya had the flu, I did not leave her bed for three days. She said I was the best nurse in Brooklyn.

title: Waiting by the Door
text: Every evening at six I sit by the door. Every evening she comes home. Every evening it is the best moment of the day.

title: Good Girl
text: Maya says it every night before she turns out the light. Good girl, Pom. Good girl.
